title: Moki&Julio: Kinect v1 as a measuring instrument (depth lattice, noise populations, capabilities)
description: Measurements and tools for one Xbox 360 Kinect (PrimeSense PS1080) via Kinect for Windows SDK 1.8. The SDK's depth output is exactly PrimeSense's published shift-to-depth table at phase 0 (259 values between 1 and 4 m, 345 in the 0.8-4 m window, matching a 2014 census), whereas libfreenect and OpenNI sit at phase 0.5, so the drivers' value sets interleave by half a step. The SDK's calibration blob, read through documented calls only, contains the PrimeSense registration block; the SDK uses it only for depth-to-colour registration, while its 3-D coordinates use a nominal pinhole. Also: three range-dependent per-pixel noise populations, a short-range temporal correlation (detrended), warm-up drift, capability confirmations (Bayer mosaic, 10-bit IR, hardware gates, extended depth, 4-channel audio, accelerometer) and a lateral-scale check against a factory-sized reference (+0.45 % to +1.74 %; no verdict by its sealed rule). Every claim has its script and status; corrections are listed first.
